title: Cohomology above the number of projective coordinates
statement:
For any commutative ring $A$, any $n\ge0$, and any
quasi-coherent module $\mathcal F$ on
$\hyperref[def-pc-projective-space-twist]{\mathbf P^n_A}$,
one has $H^q(\mathbf P^n_A,\mathcal F)=0$ for $q>n$.

proof.text: Take the standard affine covering of projective space from [def-pc-projective-space-twist] and [def-pc-proj]. The scheme is separated over Spec A, so its finite intersections are affine. Apply [lem-pc-cech-computes], in its separated affine-base specialization, to identify the homology of the module-valued Cech complex with H^q of the quasi-coherent module. Forget scalars and use the already proved comparison with the explicit abelian-group Cech complex.

Give the finite coordinate type an order by an equivalence with Fin of its cardinality. Construct the chosen intersections of [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex] as finite infima of the standard opens. The universal properties hold because morphisms of opens are inclusions. The resulting complex is degreewise identical to the explicit Cech complex: both differentials are the signed sum of the omitted-coordinate restrictions. Apply [lem-pc-alternating-cech-computes] to obtain a complex with degree-q group the product over strictly increasing maps from Fin(q+1) to the coordinate type, and an isomorphism on homology.

A strictly increasing map Fin(q+1) to the coordinate type is injective, forcing q+1 <= card(n) = d+1, contrary to q>d. The index type is therefore empty and the alternating degree-q term is the zero group. Its homology in degree q is zero because it is a subquotient of that term. Transport zero homology back along the alternating comparison and the two encoding isomorphisms, then along the affine Cech-to-H linear equivalence. This gives Subsingleton of H^q without any field or noetherian hypothesis.
